longest_story.title: The Web of Doom!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; Dr. Peter Driscoll (introduction); Tom Bailey (introduction); Brad Carter (introduction); Paul Wade (introduction); unnamed killer (villain, introduction); Mitch Rollins (villain, introduction); Joe Tyler (villain, introduction)
longest_story.synopsis: Dr. Peter Driscoll suffers from amnesia and cannot remember where he dropped a parcel with deadly microbes. Batman and Robin hopes to jog his memory by confronting him with three prisoners who served as his test subjects during the microbe research. But finding these men proves to be no easy matter: the first one stands accused of murder, the second one has gone legit and the third one is on the run.
longest_story.notes: Writer credit by Martin O'Hearn and inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Living Bat-Plane!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Dr. Philip Winters; Slant Stafford (villain)
longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn. Penciler credit confirmed by Dick Sprang. Inker credit confirmed by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: Fan-Mail of Danger!
longest_story.first_line: The fluoroscope shows that this "fan" gift is...
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Susie Smith (introduction, secretary); Ned Norton (introduction); Norton's mother (introduction); Vincent Crail (villain, forger, introduction); Crail's gang (villains, introduction for all)
longest_story.synopsis: Swamped by fan mail, Batman hires a secretary to handle all of it, who, unwittingly, causes the volume of mail to increase, thus hampering the Caped Crusader's war on crime. A threat from a forger, who has obtained an example of Batman's signature and who attempts to uncover Batman's true identity from it, has to be stopped in his tracks.
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit confirmed by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: Batman, Baby-Sitter!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Alfred Pennworth; Jane (Bruce Wayne's cousin, introduction); Junior (Jane's baby, introduction); Whitey Wills (villain, introduction); Wills' gang (villains, introduction for all)
longest_story.synopsis: Unexpectedly, Bruce's cousin Jane drops off her child for him to care for, and Bruce is forced to not only care for the child, but to fight crime as well!
longest_story.notes: Penciler credit verified by Sprang and inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Sign of the Bat!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; John Marstin (villain); Marstin's gang [Lefty; others unnamed]
longest_story.synopsis: Unable to get the evidence he needs to convict hoodlum Marstin, Batman devises a plan to make sure that Marstin and his gang see the famed but dreaded bat symbol each time they try to commit a crime...a plan which eventually allows the Caped Crusaders to nab the felon.
longest_story.notes: Inker credit verified by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: The Guardian of 100 Cities!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Roger Stanton (former actor, introduction); Shag Darnell (villain, introduction); Shag's gang (villains, introduction for all)
longest_story.synopsis: Famed replica artifacts from various movie sets, located in a field not far from Hollywood, serve as the stage as a hideout for escaped convict Shag Darnell and his thugs.
longest_story.notes: Writer credit by Martin O'Hearn, inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: His Majesty, King Batman
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; King Eric of Morania (introduction); Chancellor Zartis; Count Viras; Mayne Malan (villain, introduction); Malan's gang (villains, introduction for all)
longest_story.synopsis: A visiting royal dignitary visiting Gotham City gets an unexpected role he never expected: to play the role of Batman while the real Caped Crusader looks for a wanted felon. Unfortunately for Batman, the King doesn't want to give up that role once he gets it!
longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: Doom on Channel 14
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Marty Kirk (villain, introduction); Mugsy Burns (villain, introduction); unnamed gang members (villains, introduction for all)
longest_story.synopsis: When Batman re-enacts the capture of gangster Marty Kirk, Kirk's gang members capture the Dynamic Duo in the studio, and force officials to release Kirk from prison.
longest_story.notes: Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Return of Mister Future
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Professor Carter Nichols; Jules Verne; Simak (villain, introduction); Simak's gang (villains, introduction for all)
longest_story.synopsis: Crooks steal a secret weapon created by author Jules Verne, so the Caped Crusaders travel back in time, bring Verne back to the present, and have him design a counter weapon that will nullify his deadly weapon.
longest_story.notes:
Writer credit verifed by Martin O'Hearn, penciler credit verified by Dick Sprang and inker credit verified by Charles Paris. 

First Arnold Drake story for DC. The character Simak was possibly named for science-fiction writer Clifford D. Simak.

longest_story.title: The Golden Eggs!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; The Penguin [Oswald Cobblepot] (villain); Penguin's gang (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: Batman must stop the Fowl Felon's latest crime spree, which is based on the type of birds hatched from eggs.
longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Charles Paris.

longest_story.title: Batmantown, U.S.A.
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Mayor of Plainville; City Council of Plainville; Keene Wilder (villain, a swindler); Mr. Dane (villain, resident of Batmantown); Barsh (villain); Barsh's gang (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: When the city of Plainville decides to change its name to Batmantown in order to attract residents, Batman figures that it will draw the criminal element instead.
